# Temple Scroll Column 37 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 37 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 37:1 — "consecrate" vs. "sanctify" vs. "place My name" — qadash rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "consecrate" | Implies the initial act of setting apart |
| LOGOS | "sanctify" | Formal synonym, emphasizes ongoing holiness |
| PNEUMA | omits verb, uses "where I place My name" | Dynamic restructuring |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "consecrate." The verb qadash in the Hiphil implies a definitive act of dedication, best captured by "consecrate."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 37:6 — "skins" vs. "hides" — animal skin terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "skins" | Traditional biblical term ('orot) |
| LOGOS | "skins" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "hides" | Modern leather-working terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "skins" per EMET and LOGOS. The biblical term 'orot is consistently rendered "skins" in English Bible tradition (cf. Exodus 25:5).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 37:8 — "defile" vs. "contaminate" — chalal/tame' rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "defile" | Traditional cultic term |
| LOGOS | "defile" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "contaminate" | Modern equivalent suggesting pollution |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "defile" per EMET and LOGOS. The term carries theological weight in biblical purity discourse that "contaminate" does not.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 37:13 — "set My name" vs. "placed My name" — name theology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I have set My name upon it" | Literal sim/shum with "set" |
| LOGOS | "I have placed My name upon it" | Formal synonym |
| PNEUMA | "I have placed My name on it" | Same verb, shorter preposition |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "I have set My name upon it." The Deuteronomistic name-theology formula is traditionally rendered with "set" in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 37:15 — "abominable" vs. "detestable" — to'evah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "abominable" | Traditional rendering of to'evah |
| LOGOS | "abominable" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "detestable" | Modern synonym |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "abominable" per EMET and LOGOS. Consistent with traditional rendering of to'evah throughout the project.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
